tier_reason: PR #2745 (merged 2020-09-22 by garazdawi) states the estone, JSON and RabbitMQ gains of the JIT over the BEAM interpreter verbatim as in the record, but names no CPU, compiler or flags and links no run scripts, so these are first-party numbers without methodology.

corrections.caveats: Numbers are from the description of the original BeamAsm merge PR (merged 2020-09-22, shipped in OTP 24); hardware, compiler and flags are not stated, and the exact runs are not reproducible from the page. The project's own BeamAsm design doc (erts/emulator/internal_doc/BeamAsm.md) says to expect 'anything from no difference to up to four times as fast' and that very short-lived small scripts can be slower than the interpreter. Baseline is the project's own interpreter (still buildable with --disable-jit or FLAVOR=emu), not one of PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot. JIT only on x86-64 and AArch64 (asmjit). The entry is the JIT inside the much larger Erlang/OTP repository (code in erts/emulator/beam/jit/).

notes: Claim matches PR #2745 exactly; off-baseline for the jits category (own interpreter, not PyPy/LuaJIT/V8/HotSpot) and no methodology. Metadata checked on github.com: Apache-2.0, 12.4k stars, not archived, last commit 2026-10-06 on master.

tier_reason: README and the Blink 1.0 release notes give first-party '2x faster than qemu-x86_64' claims (SSE math, GCC cc1 compiling Hello World) with no named suite, QEMU version, CPU, compiler or flags and no benchmark directory in the repo; numbers without methodology are C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'Blink goes 2x faster than qemu-x86_64 on some benchmarks, such as SSE integer / floating point math. Blink is also much faster at running ephemeral programs such as compilers.' Blink 1.0 release notes (2023-06-04, https://github.com/jart/blink/releases/tag/1.0.0): 'Blink has a snappy JIT that in some cases goes 2x faster than Qemu for use-cases like ephemeral programs' and, from a screenshot of GCC's cc1, 'Blink is able to compile Hello World at least 2x faster'. README also says Blink 'usually uses 40% less peak resident memory than Qemu' and that disabling the JIT makes it '10x slower'.
corrections.caveats: First-party claims only: '2x on some benchmarks' with no named benchmark suite, QEMU version, compiler flags or CPU; the release-notes comparison is a screenshot of one cc1 Hello World compile. No benchmark directory in the repo (top level: blink/, build/, test/, third_party/, tool/). Wins are stated only for some workloads, so Blink is not claimed faster than QEMU in general. Baseline is not one of PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot.

notes: Claim confirmed in README; the release notes add the cc1 Hello World 2x comparison (still first-party, no methodology). Metadata checked on github.com: ISC, 7.6k stars, last commit 2025-12-10 (active).

tier_reason: The README's '5-10x faster than the interpreter alone' is a first-party claim against the project's own interpreter with no workload, CPU or flags. The peer-reviewed EuroSys 2026 paper reports 3.3x over QEMU-TCG on RISC-V, but only its abstract was seen (search snippet; dl.acm.org EGRESS_BLOCKED, no PDF found on GitHub), so it does not lift the tier yet.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: 'With DynaRec for Arm, RISC-V and LoongArch platforms, Box64 achieves a speed boost 5-10x faster than the interpreter alone.' EuroSys 2026 paper 'Practical and Efficient x86-64 Emulation on RISC-V' (Tan, Liu, Chevalier, Chen, Liu, Fu; https://doi.org/10.1145/3767295.3803574), abstract (snippet only): average performance penalty of less than 40% versus native execution and outperforms QEMU-TCG by 3.3x on RISC-V.
corrections.caveats: README baseline is the project's own interpreter, not an independent incumbent; no workload, CPU or flags named. The stronger comparison (3.3x over QEMU-TCG, RISC-V only) is in the peer-reviewed EuroSys 2026 paper co-authored by the Box64 author, seen only as an abstract snippet because dl.acm.org is blocked and no PDF copy was found on GitHub; that paper could support tier B against QEMU once read. The linked box86.org game-performance analysis (2021) was not opened. Baseline is not one of PyPy, LuaJIT, V8, HotSpot.

notes: README claim confirmed verbatim; README also cites a EuroSys 2026 paper whose abstract (snippet only) claims 3.3x over QEMU-TCG on RISC-V. If the orchestrator reaches the paper PDF, consider re-baselining to QEMU-TCG and retiering to B. Metadata checked on github.com: MIT, 5.7k stars, last commit 2026-10-06 (active).
